voyage.name: Teatro San Gallo
voyage.content: Half-hour documentary based on the BBC series Francesco's Venice - an 'amazing film that puts the spectacular beauty of this great city in historical context'. Film in English, audioguides in Italian, Russian and Spanish.

voyage.name: E Rosa Salva
voyage.content: One of the favorites is the mini-chain "E Rosa Salva", with three locations in the center - on C. Fiubera (from Piazza San Marco, take the underpass in the middle of the arcade, cross the bridge and take second right off C. Fabbri), Merceria S. Salvadore (off the campo of the same name), and right on Campo San Zanipolo (to the right of the church looking from the canal); the last one is a gelateria as well. For your

voyage.name: Domus Ciliota
voyage.content: A 5-10 minute walk from San Marco's Square. The hotel has over fifty clean, basic, air-conditioned rooms all with shower and WC. The 24-hr reception is English speaking. There is an area for leaving baggage after you've checked out. Single rooms are €70-85 and doubles are €100-110 including breakfast.

voyage.name: Hotel Ala
voyage.address: Campo Santa Maria dei Gigli, San Marco 2494
voyage.content: Eggs and broiled tomatoes with cheese for breakfast. Rooms were a typical size but clean, comfortable and quiet. They have turndown service at night, a pleasant surprise.

voyage.name: Hotel All'Angelo Venice
voyage.content: Run by the same family since 1924 in a 17th-century building close to St Marks Basilica. Comfortable and stylishly decorated rooms with a double somewhere in the region of €150.

voyage.name: Hotel Antico Panada
voyage.content: Has rooms decorated in an 18th-century Venetian style.

voyage.name: Hotel Becher
voyage.content: This 18th-century hotel enhanced by the most modern amenities, charming atmosphere and impeccable service. Single rooms from €70, doubles €110 and triples from €170.

voyage.name: Hotel Firenze Venice
voyage.price: Rooms start at around €120 a double/twin
voyage.content: On a side street of Piazza San Marco, and offers bright and comfortable rooms.

voyage.name: Hotel Lisbona Venice
voyage.content: Just in front of Piazza San Marco, three star rooms decorated in the grand Venetian style. Double rooms are usually around €140.

voyage.name: Hotel Montecarlo Venice
voyage.price: Rooms start at around €130 a double
voyage.content: 3-star superior rooms and services one hundred yards from the entrance to Basilica San Marco.

voyage.name: Hotel San Giorgio
voyage.price: Single rooms from €60, doubles from €90, triples from €120
voyage.address: Rio Terà della Mandola, San Marco 3781
voyage.content: The hotel is between Campo Sant'Angelo and Campo Manin in an antique Gothic palace bought by Mariano Fortuny.

voyage.name: Hotel San Moise Venice
voyage.price: Starting in the region of €120-140 for a double room
voyage.content: 3-star hotel behind Piazza San Marco and the Basilica.

voyage.name: Pagan Luxury House
voyage.content: According to their website, there is a €10 per night discount for booking directly with them.

voyage.name: Hotel Flora
voyage.content: Garden, free Wi-Fi, homemade buffet breakfast, fitness centre.

voyage.name: Novecento Boutique Hotel
voyage.content: Has 9 rooms featuring original furniture and tapestries from both the Mediterranean and the Far East.

voyage.name: Locanda Orseolo
voyage.content: A 3-minute walk from St. Peter's Square, operated by a multi-lingual Venetian family who offer impeccable concierge service. Room rates are generally €150 to €200.

voyage.name: Corte 1321
voyage.content: Large spacious rooms with double sink bathrooms ensure a comfortable stay. Lovely courtyard for dining is made memorable with local birds strutting and cooing.

voyage.name: Hotel Marconi Venice
voyage.content: The hotel overlooks the Grand Canal and famous Rialto Bridge. It has been a hotel since the 1930 and has a very interesting art deco style, with rooms going for around €150, or for a little more with a canal view.

voyage.name: Hotel al Sole
voyage.content: Hotel is in a noble palace built in the beginning of the 15th century, a short distance from Piazzale Roma.

voyage.name: Hotel Basilea Venice
voyage.price: Double rooms are usually €100-160 depending on season
voyage.content: Across the Grand Canal from Santa Lucia Train Station. Located in a quiet Calle.

voyage.name: Hotel Doge Venice
voyage.price: Double rooms start from €57. Family apartment for three people €97
voyage.address: Lista Vecchia dei Bari, Santa Croce 1222
voyage.content: Three-star accommodation of Venice. It is in the northern part of the city, in front of the train station and presents 10 bedrooms – single, double and twin, some with a shared bathroom - and one apartment.

voyage.name: Hotel Alla Salute
voyage.content: A 16th-century palazzo, a stone's throw from Piazza San Marco. It has been the house of the famous poet Ezra Pound. Pretty comfortable and quiet budget hotel. Garden for breakfast.

voyage.name: Belle Arti Hotel Venice
voyage.price: Double €220. Breakfast included for those who book online
voyage.content: Elegant three-star hotel. 67 guestrooms divided in double, triple and quadruple with en suite services, bathroom kit and modern services.

voyage.name: Hotel Palazzo Guardi
voyage.content: A stone's throw from the Accademia, is this noble Venetian palace, rooms equipped with all comforts.

voyage.name: Hotel Cà D'Oro
voyage.content: The hotel is in a quiet corner of Cannaregio district, 5 minutes walk from the Rialto Bridge.

voyage.name: Jewish Ghetto of Venice
voyage.content: While racial and ethnic neighborhoods had existed prior to the Venetian Ghetto, Venice's ghetto was the first "ghetto" (coming from a Venetian word for the Iron Foundry that had been on the site) and "ghetto" eventually came to mean any neighborhood that was made up of a single ethnic/racial group. Today, Jewish life is still very active in the ghetto, and elsewhere in Venice, and is home to five synagogues. Visiting

voyage.name: Jewish Museum
voyage.price: Entrance: adults €3, reduced €2. Entrance with guided tours to synagogues: adults €8.50, reduced €7
voyage.hours: 1 Jun-30 Sep: 10:00-19:00; 1 Oct-31 May: 10:00-18:00. Closed on Sat (Shabbat), during Jewish festivities, on 25 Dec, 1 Jan and 1 May
voyage.content: Objects related to the social life of the Jewish community, in two synagogues of the 16th century.

voyage.name: Galleria Giorgio Franchetti Ca' d'Oro
voyage.content: A collection of paintings and statues in a former palace from the 15th century. One of the best examples of Gothic architecture in Venice, sculptures, bronzes, paintings of Mantegna, Giorgione and Titian, Flemish and Dutch paintings.

voyage.name: Oratorio dei Crociferi
voyage.hours: Fri Sat 10:00-13:00 and 14:00-17:00, otherwise only by reservation
voyage.content: Small oratory facing the old monastery dei Crociferi, painting circle by Palma the Younger.

voyage.name: Santa Maria di Nazareth Church
voyage.alt: Chiesa di Santa Maria di Nazareth
voyage.content: Also known as Church of the Scalzi (Chiesa degli Scalzi), being the seat in the city of the Discalced Carmelites religious order (scalzi in Italian means "barefoot"). Built in the mid 17th century to the designs of Baldassarre Longhena and completed in the last decades of that century.

voyage.name: Madonna dell'Orto Church
voyage.content: With the grave and 10 paintings of Jacopo Robusti (Tintoretto) (1578-1594), and his tomb.

voyage.name: I Gesuiti
voyage.content: Also known as Church of Santa Maria Assunta, the current structure dates back to 1729.

voyage.name: Scuola dell'Angelo Custode
voyage.content: The only Lutheran church in Venice.

voyage.name: San Michele Cemetery
voyage.content: Cemetery established following Napoleon Bonaparte's edict of 1804, part of the European circuit of monumental cemeteries. The Russian ballet director Sergei Diaghilev, the Austrian physicist Christan Doppler, the American poet Ezra Pound, the Russian composer Igor Stravinsky and the German-Italian composer Ermanno Wolf-Ferrari are buried in San Michele Cemetery.

voyage.name: Santa Maria dei Miracoli
voyage.content: A perfect jewel box church, simple in form but ornamented with fine exterior marble facings.

voyage.name: Teatro Malibran
voyage.content: Teatro Malibran was built in 1678, and is now part of La Fenice. Tickets for opera, ballet, and symphony performances are available at La Fenice, various locations around the city, or by phone .

voyage.name: Venice Casino
voyage.price: Entrance €10, free if you are booked at selected hotels
voyage.content: The oldest gambling house in the world, founded in 1638. The building dates back to the 15th century.

voyage.name: Orsoni Furnace
voyage.content: One of the last industries left in Venice, the Orsoni Furnace produces fine glass panels and mosaics using the same technique since 1888. The small factory can only be visited on certain dates.

voyage.name: Crepes House by PePe
voyage.content: Savory and sweet crepes

voyage.name: Al Timon
voyage.content: Warm and local atmosphere in this little osteria where they serve great Italian vintages by the glass. If you're adventurous, try their tasty tripe. Good music inside, some table by the canal in the summer. Reservations on evenings is essential.

voyage.name: La Colombina
voyage.content: Artfully presented Venetian cuisine

voyage.name: Trattoria Alla Fontana
voyage.content: Warm canalside restaurant

voyage.name: Ristorante Casa Bonita
voyage.content: Generous portions of pasta and seafood

voyage.name: Vino Vero
voyage.content: Small wine bar with excellent selection, away from the tourist crowds. Outdoor seating next to one of the canals.

voyage.name: Al Parlamento
voyage.content: Another small bar, away from the main tourist arteries. Serves spritz, cocktails and beer with a view of the Cannaregio canal.

voyage.name: Bed and Breakfast Ca'Dor
voyage.price: Rooms about 55 EUR in low-season, 100 EUR in high season
voyage.content: Venetian style rooms in the centre, 3 minutes from Rialto's Bridge.

voyage.name: Alloggi Agli Artisti
voyage.price: From €50 to €90 for a double room, depending on the season
voyage.content: Guests can choose between rooms with bathroom en suite (with hairdryer), and rooms with sharing bathroom on the floor (cheaper).

voyage.name: Antica Casa Carettoni Venice
voyage.content: Close to Santa Lucia Train Station and the waterbus stops. 3 star hotel in an old convent offers accommodation starting at around €120-130 for a double room.

voyage.name: Ca' Amadi
voyage.content: In the old town centre, close to the famous Rialto Bridge. This 13th-century palace was once home to Marco Polo. Décor is keeping with the period, and the rooms are utterly charming. Original wall frescoes from the 1400s adorn the hotel.

voyage.name: Continental Hotel Venice
voyage.content: Three-star hotel in the Jewish Ghetto. A historic building belonged to a noble family, with 93 bedrooms (€95-194) capable to host any kind of guests.

voyage.name: Ca' Gottardi
voyage.content: Antico Palazzo Gottardi stands in Strada Nuova, between two buildings that look down onto the Canal Grande.

voyage.name: Hotel Cà D'Oro
voyage.content: The hotel is in a quiet corner of Cannaregio district, 5 minutes walk from the Rialto Bridge.

voyage.name: Hotel il Mercante di Venezia
voyage.content: Just off the Lista di Spagna by the Grand Canal, excellent access to the Station (Santa Lucia) and the waterbuses. Delicately appointed rooms from around €145.

voyage.name: Hotel Nazionale Venice
voyage.price: €80 for a single and €160 for a family
voyage.content: Three-star accommodation with 90 bedrooms divided in single, double, twin, triple and family, 100 metres away from the train station of Santa Lucia.

voyage.name: Palazzo Cendon - Il Piano Nobile
voyage.content: Nice small hotel in good area with a few restaurants and bars.

voyage.name: Hotel Giorgione
voyage.content: In the centre, 10 minutes from Piazza San Marco, it was transformed into a hotel at the beginning of the 19th century and has been managed by the same family ever since.

voyage.name: Bridge of Sighs
voyage.content: Connecting the Doge's Palace with the prison. Persons convicted in the palace were passing to prison here, seeing the last of Venice before going into the dark prison area with no daylight. You can pass the bridge yourself during a visit to the Doge's Palace or view it from outside from the Ponte della Paglia.

voyage.name: Napoleonic Gardens
voyage.content: They are the largest green area in the historic center and are home to the Venice International Art Exhibition. The gardens contain lush vegetation, among which the various twentieth-century architectures of the pavilions are organised, mostly around a central avenue from which smaller paths branch off, characteristic for their shape and each one bearing the name of the nation hosted.

voyage.name: San Giovanni e Paolo
voyage.content: A fine, huge Dominican church with the tombs of many Doges. It shares its piazza with the fine Renaissance façade of the Scuola San Marco and an equestrian statue of the mercenary captain Bartolomeo Colleoni (see below).

voyage.name: Santa Maria della Pietà
voyage.content: A church that used to house an orphanage and hospital in the 18th century, it is known among classical music enthusiasts as the church where the Catholic priest and composer Antonio Vivaldi worked for most of his career.

voyage.name: S. Francesco della Vigna
voyage.address: Campo San Francesco della Vigna, Castello

voyage.name: S. Maria Formosa
voyage.content: The first church dedicated to "Mary of the Forms" was built on this spot in the VII century, when the Virgin ordered bishop Magnus to erect one, appearing to him as an exceedingly shapely woman. The current building, planned by Codussi, dates from the early XV century.

voyage.name: Basilica di San Pietro di Castello
voyage.content: Venice cathedral up to 1807, when the see was transferred to San Marco.

voyage.name: Museo Diocesano
voyage.content: Religious furniture and objects from now demolished churches and convents, one of the most appealing Romanesque cloisters of Venice.

voyage.name: Museo Storico Navale
voyage.content: Collection of relics from the Serenissima Republic of Venice, the Italian navy, and the ancient Arsenale shipyards, miniature models, uniforms and stadarts, collection of sea shells. The main building of the Naval Historical Museum (Riva S. Biasio) is closed for renovation works. It's possible to visit the Ships Pavilion in rio della Tana, Castello 2162 (close to the Naval Museum).

voyage.name: Fondazione Querini Stampalia
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00; closed Mon, Dec 25 and 26, Jan 1
voyage.content: Residence-museum of the Querini-Stampa family, library, picture gallery, furniture and household objects from the 16th cent onwards, important paintings by Bellini, Palma, Ricci, Tiepolo and Longhi.

voyage.name: Byzantine Pictures Museum (Greek Institute)
voyage.content: Collection of Greek, Cretan and Venetian icons of the 14th to 18th century.

voyage.name: Palazzo Grimani
voyage.content: A jewel of Renaissance architecture that was opened as a Venetia civic museum in 2008, collections of paintings, archaeological collection of Greek and Roman artefacts, temporary exhibitions.

voyage.name: Scuola Dalmatina di San Giorgio e Trifone
voyage.content: Famous painting cycle by Vittore Carpaccio depicting the lives of St.George, Tryphon and Jerome.

voyage.name: ASAC Library
voyage.alt: Biblioteca ASAC - Archivo Storico Arti Contemporanee della Biennale di Venezia
voyage.content: An annex at the Biennale gardens where the Biennale keeps records related to the Biennale exhibitions and to 20th century art, from 1895 onwards.

voyage.name: Equestrian statue of Bartolomeo Colleoni
voyage.content: The famous condottiere (1395–1475) had a long and remunerative career as captain of a mercenary army fighting for (or against, depending on the pay) the Republic, but died without an heir (8 daughters did not count) and bequeathed most of his significant wealth to Venice - on the condition that the grateful populace erect a monument to him in front of San Marco. The crafty council fulfilled the condition, with one de

voyage.name: Monuement for Gentile Bellini
voyage.content: Venetian painter and official portraitist of the Doges (1439-1507), tomb.

voyage.name: Monument for Giovanni Caboto
voyage.content: Venetian explorer of North America who worked for the British (c. 1450-c. 1500).

voyage.name: Giuseppe Verdi
voyage.content: Composer of operas; Italian nationalist and national hero (1813-1901).

voyage.name: Richard Wagner
voyage.content: German opera composer (1813-1883).

voyage.name: Chiesa della Pietà
voyage.content: Between 1703 and 1740, Antonio Vivaldi taught the orchestra of the girls in the orphanage here, writing unparalleled music for them. Frequent concerts of his Four Seasons by a Baroque ensemble.

voyage.name: I Tre Mercanti
voyage.content: Here you can find a special selection of the best Italian food and drinks products. Well known for their amazing single portion Tiramisù. If you don't feel like shopping you can always browse the shop and ask cooking tips and the history of products. They can supply yachts, make exclusive gift packages or hampers for companies, and ship worldwide.

voyage.name: Libreria Acqua Alta
voyage.content: Cozy antiquarian bookshop with many odd and specialized books. The owner is fond of cats, so expect to make new feral friends while you browse the shelves and stacks (or the gondola in the middle of the back room).

voyage.name: Cip ciap
voyage.content: Also sells delicious takeaway pizza by the slice (or slab) at similar prices. They also serve very tasty mini pizzas per kilogram.

voyage.name: Osteria Alla Rampa
voyage.content: A bistro

voyage.name: Al Vecio Canton
voyage.content: This small and atmospheric restaurant/pizzeria will absolutely enchant you. Famous for its traditional style pizza and seafood pasta, you will not only get it all at affordable prices (pizza from €7.50, pasta from €10, wine from €5/half litre), but you're also served by a most friendly and hearty staff. They top it off with a free home made digestivo (mostly vodka and lemon) at the end of your meal, just to make 100%

voyage.name: Al Giardinetto
voyage.content: Just behind the Piazza San Marco, this restaurant has a large private courtyard welcoming guests during good season. Seafood courses and Venetian specialities are served by Severino family.

voyage.name: Pub Taverna L'Olandese Volante
voyage.content: Located between the Rialto Bridge and Piazza San Marco. During the summertime there are tables outside when you can easily sit and rest after a day of wandering around this marvelous city. What is more, during the day pasta and other typical dishes are served at a budget price.

voyage.name: Locanda Sant'Anna
voyage.content: One star. Provides a family atmosphere with modern comforts. Quiet hotel with secure courtyard and some rooms with a canal view (for a higher price) overlooking the Isola di San Pietro. Common balcony over the canal. Includes typical Italian breakfast from 08:00-09:30 with coffee or hot chocolate and rolls, croissants, and toast. Easily accessible from the main bus/train station by vaporetto to stop 'S. Pietro' or 'G

voyage.name: Ca' Bauta
voyage.content: Housed in a 15th-century building, this quaint hotel has very spacious rooms with high ceilings and is adorned with stylish furniture and fittings. Has a friendly, multilingual staff who are always eager to assist you in planning tours, booking concert tickets, and making restaurant reservations. Rates from €70 per night.

voyage.name: Ca' Valeri
voyage.content: Residence where an atmosphere of charm and comfort defines an ambience of class.

voyage.name: Hotel Ai Due Principi
voyage.content: Boutique hotel.

voyage.name: Hotel Canaletto Venice
voyage.content: Along a scenic canal close to St. Mark’s Basilica. Decorated and furnished in the traditional Venetian manner, this hotel offers excellent service and rooms for two that start at around €110.

voyage.name: Hotel Commercio e Pellegrino
voyage.price: Single rooms from €80, doubles from €100 including taxes and breakfast
voyage.content: Comfortable hotel in the centre, easy to reach by public transport and 2 minutes on foot to Saint Mark’s Square.

voyage.name: Residenza Cà Bauta
voyage.content: Few steps from Campo ss. Giovanni e Paolo, one of the most spectacular place of Venice. Double rooms are usually around €100-160 depending on season.

voyage.name: Residenza Cá Malipiero Venice
voyage.content: An historic building of the 16th century with a large selection of elegant single, double rooms and suites, capable to host up to four people and equipped with the best modern services expected by a three-star guest house.

voyage.name: Hotel Tiepolo
voyage.content: Small and elegant design hotel in the historic centre, a few steps away from Saint Mark's Square.

voyage.name: I Gesuati
voyage.content: 18th-century Dominican church on the Giudecca canal. The classical style building has a well-lit interior and is exceptional in preserving its original layout and Rococo decoration intact. The church and almost all its sculpture and paintings were created within a 30-year period: construction began in 1725, the church was consecrated in 1743, and the last sculptural decoration was in place by 1755.

voyage.name: S. Maria della Salute
voyage.content: As a votive offering for the city's deliverance from the Black Plague, the church was designed in the then fashionable Baroque style. Construction began in 1631. Most of the objects of art housed in the church bear references to the Black Death. Because of its location between the Grand Canal and the Giudecca Canal, its dome was an important addition to the Venice skyline and soon became emblematic of the city, appea

voyage.name: Church of Saint Sebastian
voyage.content: 16th-century Roman Catholic church, houses a cycle of paintings by the artist Paolo Veronese as well as paintings by Tintoretto and Titian. Includes the tomb of Paolo Veronese, a painter from Verona whose career was in Venice (1528-1588).

voyage.name: Santa Maria del Carmelo church
voyage.alt: Chiesa di Santa Maria dei Carmini
voyage.content: Large 14th-century Roman Catholic church.

voyage.name: San Nicolò dei Mendicoli church
voyage.alt: Chiesa di San Nicolò dei Mendicoli

voyage.name: Punta della Dogana
voyage.hours: Wed-Mon 10:00 to 19:00, closed Tue and Dec 24
voyage.content: Former customs house, centre for contemporary art, permanent exhibition of works from the François Pinault Collection. Renovation by world renowned architect Tadao Ando.

voyage.name: Ca' Rezzonico - Museum of 18th Century Venice
voyage.hours: Nov-Mar: 10:00-17:00, Apr-Oct: 10:00-18:00; closed Dec 25, Jan 1, May 1
voyage.content: Museum of the 18th century in Venice - attempts to revive the domestic atmosphere of Venetian nobilities. Furniture, interior decoration, paintings by Guardi, Canaletto, Tiepolo. On the third floor important paintings of the Venetian school. A MUVE museum.

voyage.name: Gallerie dell'Accademia
voyage.hours: Mon 08:15-14:00, Tue-Sun 08:15-19:15 (ticket office closes 1 hr before)
voyage.content: Venice's most significant art museum which is also one of Italy's best. Among the most important paintings in the Accademia are: Gentile Bellini: Procession on St. Mark’s Square (1496) and Miracle of the Cross at the Bridge of S. Lorenzo (1500), Giovanni Bellini: Pieta (1500), Jacopo Bellini: Madonna with Child and Cherubs (ca. 1450), Paris Bordenone: A fisherman presents the ring of St. Mark to the doge (ca. 1535),

voyage.name: Gallery Palazzo Cini
voyage.content: Former residence of Italian industrialist Vittorio Cini who amassed large collection of Italian art. The gallery houses a collection of 15th and 16th cent paintings from Tuscany and Ferrara, period furniture, silver, ivory and ceramic objects.

voyage.name: The Peggy Guggenheim Museum
voyage.price: Adult €17, seniors (over 65 years) €15, students (25 years and under with valid student ID) €10, youth 10-18 €9, 9 and younger free
voyage.hours: Wed-Mon 10:00-18:00. Closed on Tuesdays and on 25 December. Open on national holidays (including Tuesdays)
voyage.content: Offers a personal collection of modern art collected by Peggy Guggenheim. Peggy was an American married to modern artist Max Ernst, and funded a number of his contemporaries. The gallery includes a sculpture garden and works by Picasso, Kandinsky, Gorky, Tanguy, Duchamp, Pollock, Dali, and Mondrian.

voyage.name: Scuola Grande dei Carmini
voyage.content: Painting cycles dedicated to the Madonna del Carmine, canvases by Tiepolo and Padoviano.

voyage.name: Le Macchine di Leonardo a Venezia
voyage.content: An exhibition in the Chiesa di San Barnaba showing around forty models of machines reproduced from Leonardo's codices. Some of the exhibits are interactive and copies of the codices are available for further reading. The church is an attraction in itself: it's the one under which Indiana Jones finds catacombs in The Last Crusade, by the way).

voyage.name: Northern Giudecca canal walk
voyage.content: It's a long and sunny walk along the Giudecca canal, protected during winter time from cold northerly winds for being exposed to south and shielded by buildings. You might find interesting to see how a gondola is made, stopping by the Squero (Venetian for small ship yard) across a canal near San Trovaso Church. It's one of the few still in business in town. With some luck, you'll see some gondole through various manu

voyage.name: Southern Giudecca canal walk
voyage.content: Like the northern version you walk along the entire Giudecca canal, but in this case on the Giudecca island.

voyage.name: Squero di San Trovaso
voyage.content: Squero is Venetian for small ship yard.

voyage.name: The Avogaria Theatre
voyage.content: The smallest theatre in Venice, housed in an unassuming former workshop.

voyage.name: Pasticceria Tonolo
voyage.content: Hugely popular patisserie which has been around since late 19th century. Their cake with crystallized fruits and marzipan cake are must-tries. While they do offer a few seats you are much better off taking the pastries with you. Be there early to beat the queues.

voyage.name: Pizza al volo
voyage.content: Sells superb pizza by the (extremely large) slice in Campo Santa Margherita for approximately €1.80 a slice, €5 a whole pizza. It is by the fresh fish stall under a green awning.

voyage.name: La Foca
voyage.content: Pizza

voyage.name: La Bitta
voyage.content: This busy but friendly restaurant is in the more studenty area of Dorsoduro, and attracts a mixture of locals and tourists. They have some excellent Italian dishes, which are reflected in the prices, plus they have a great selection of wines.

voyage.name: Osteria Ai Do Farai
voyage.content: Serves fresh shell fish. Taste their spaghetti al dente with razor shells.

voyage.name: Osteria Enoteca Ai Artisti
voyage.content: An excellent restaurant, small but comfortable with a few tables alongside a tiny canal. Food is fresh and delicious, not too expensive. Large selection of wines. Menu changing daily.

voyage.name: Chet Bar
voyage.content: The closest thing to a dive bar you'll find in Venice, except that the cocktails actually are pretty good.

voyage.name: Il Caffè Rosso
voyage.content: Small but hugely popular café at Campo Santa Margherita. Serves coffee and sandwiches during the day, and excellent spritz during nights.

voyage.name: Cantine del Vino gia Schiavi
voyage.content: Inventive and delicious cicchetti; pile a plate with what you like, and the staff will pour you a glass of wine to match the selection. If it's too crowded inside, step out and find a space by the canal. A large and carefully curated selection of wines and spirits for purchase by the bottle. Joseph Brodsky, the American Nobel Prize winning poet and essayist, buried on San Michele, was a regular anytime he came to Ven

voyage.name: Ca' Della Corte
voyage.content: A comfortable B&B in a quiet area. Warm and personal welcome. Breakfast (served in the room) could be improved (by going to pasticceria Tonolo and bringing your own cakes, e.g.).

voyage.name: Ca' Zose
voyage.content: A quiet street off S.M. Salute, by the S.M. Giglio traghetto (when it's operational, 50 cents will get you to S. Marco), within easy walk of either Accademia or the Zattere (no need to brave the hordes of tourists on the #1 line, take the #52 from bus or train station). The helpful staff speaks Italian, English, French and Veneto. 10% discount on rates if paid in cash - ask Walentina, the proprietress. All rooms are

voyage.name: Locanda Gaffaro
voyage.content: In a picturesque court near Piazzale Roma.

voyage.name: Belmond Hotel Cipriani
voyage.content: Opened in 1958 and long considered one of the leading luxury hotels of the world.

voyage.name: Rialto Bridge
voyage.content: The bridge has become one of Venice's most recognizable icons and has a history that spans over 800 years. Today's Rialto Bridge was completed in 1591 and was used to replace a wooden bridge that collapsed in 1524.

voyage.name: Campo San Polo
voyage.content: A large campo (square), one of the most popular Carnival venues and also used for open-air concerts and screenings during the Venice Film Festival.

voyage.name: Scuola Grande di San Rocco
voyage.content: A masterpiece of Tintoretto, this guild house is an exquisite example of Mannerist art at its best. In order to allow a comfortable admiration of the detailed ceiling, mirrors are offered to the visitors. Cycles of allegories, life and passion of Christ, scenes from the Old and New Testament.

voyage.name: Scuola Grande di San Giovanni Evangelista
voyage.content: Monumental staircase by Codussi, splendid San Giovanni Salon, Oratory of the Cross with precious reliquiaries.

voyage.name: House of Carlo Goldoni
voyage.alt: Casa di Carlo Goldoni, Centro di Studi Teatrali
voyage.hours: Apr-Oct: Thu-Tue 10:00-17:00; Nov-Mar: Thu-Tue 10:00-16:00; closed Jan 1, May 1, Dec 25
voyage.content: Birthplace of Venice's most famous playwright. Museum, library and theater studies center. A MUVE museum.

voyage.name: Leonardo da Vinci Museum Venice
voyage.content: Small museum dedicated to the life and work of Leonardo da Vinci.

voyage.name: San Giacomo di Rialto
voyage.content: This church is possibly the oldest church in Venice built around 421. It is most recognized for its 15th-century clock above the entrance of the church. It is also recognized for the red pillars and beautiful gold accents around the church itself.

voyage.name: Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari
voyage.alt: Basilica dei Frai, often just referred to as the Frari
voyage.hours: Mon-Fri 09:00-18:00, Sun and holidays 13:00-18:00. Last admission 30 min before closing time
voyage.content: The big friary church, fine example of Venetian Gothic architecture, with fine monuments and paintings of Titian, Belliniand Donatello, among which the famous 'Assunta' by Titian.

voyage.name: Funerary monument of Claudio Monteverdi
voyage.content: Tomb, composer (1567-1643) and champion of the early Baroque seconda pratica and then-new genre of opera.

voyage.name: State Archive
voyage.content: One of the largest archives in the world, in an old Franciscan monastery. Manuscripts, texts and documents related to the history of the Venetian Serenissima.

voyage.name: Rialto Market
voyage.content: This vegetable and fish market has been running for hundreds of years, an essential stop for home cooks in central Venice.

voyage.name: Atelier Marega
voyage.content: A hand-made mask and costume shop.

voyage.name: Fanny
voyage.content: Hundreds of leather gloves in all colours.

voyage.name: Francis Model
voyage.content: Locally made leather bags. Exceptional craftsmanship. There are reports that some travellers were cheated in this store, by being told that transaction didn't occur while using their credit card, and demanded cash while in fact transaction did occur properly and thus having made the travellers pay for the same item twice.

voyage.name: Pizza 2000
voyage.content: Pizza takeout

voyage.name: Ostaria dai Zemei
voyage.content: Down home cooking with Venezian style tapas

voyage.name: Antico Forno
voyage.content: A pizzeria

voyage.name: Acqua e Mais
voyage.content: Small plates

voyage.name: Farini
voyage.content: A bakery

voyage.name: Ristorante Casa Cappellari
voyage.content: Traditional Venetian cuisine with a warm atmosphere

voyage.name: Antica Osteria Ruga Rialto
voyage.content: Seafood specialties

voyage.name: Farini
voyage.content: A bistro

voyage.name: Cantina Do Mori
voyage.content: Venetian tapas

voyage.name: Cantina Do Spade
voyage.content: Venetian cuisine

voyage.name: Antico Dolo
voyage.content: An old seafood restaurant close to Rialto bridge: food comes from the adjacent Rialto Market daily. A complete dinner excluding wines could cost €35 each more or less.

voyage.name: Trattoria Antiche Carampane
voyage.content: In the heart of Venice, steps away from the Rialto Bridge, is this renowned restaurant where distinguished Venetian cuisine is served in a familiar setting.

voyage.name: Gelateria Il Doge
voyage.content: Excellent ice cream, all made on the premises (a rarity in Venice). Plenty of vegan options.

voyage.name: La Bottiglia
voyage.content: A small wine bar with excellent reviews. They offer a small but constantly changing selection of wines, complemented by excellent Italian street food and snacks.

voyage.name: San Simeone Piccolo
voyage.content: The last church built in Venice. One of the things that it is recognized for is the fact that they celebrate Tridentine Mass on Sundays. It is also recognized for its dome because it is used to make the church look taller than it is and the dome itself is entirely covered with lead sheet.

voyage.name: San Giacomo dell'Orio Church
voyage.content: Founded in the 9th century, the current church was built in 1225.

voyage.name: Tolentini Church
voyage.alt: Chiesa di San Nicolò da Tolentino
voyage.content: Historic church completed in 1714.

voyage.name: Natural History Museum
voyage.content: 11 exhibition halls with sections on palaeontology, explorations and nature. A MUVE museum.

voyage.name: Mocenigo Palace Museum
voyage.alt: Museo di Palazzo Mocenigo, Centro Studi die Storia del Tessuto e del Costume
voyage.hours: Apr-Oct: 10:00-17:00, Nov-Mar: 10:00-16:00; closed Mon, Dec 26, Jan 1, May 1
voyage.content: A collection of clothes dating from the 18th century. Splendid interior. Collection of dresses and accessories, fabrics, books, figurines in various period costumes. A MUVE museum.

voyage.name: Ca' Pesaro - International Modern Art Gallery
voyage.price: Adults €14, reduced €11.50 (valid for both museums in the Ca' Pesaro)
voyage.hours: Nov-Mar: 10:00-17:00, Apr-Oct: 10:00-18:00, closed Dec 25, Jan 1, May 1
voyage.content: Modern art collection, paintings of the 19th and 20th century. A MUVE museum.

voyage.name: Ca' Pesaro - Museum of Oriental Art
voyage.alt: Museo d'arte Orientale di Ca Pesaro
voyage.price: Adults €14, reduced €11.50 (valid for both museums in the Ca' Pesaro)
voyage.hours: Nov-Mar 10:00 to 17:00, Apr-Oct: 10 :00-18:00, closed Mon, Dec 25, Jan 1, May 1
voyage.content: Beautiful palace housing the gallery of modern art focusing on Italian art in the 19th century as well as the Marco Polo Museum, a rich collection mainly of Asian exhibits (fabrics, clothes, armours, porcelain). A MUVE museum.

voyage.name: Giardini Papadopoli
voyage.content: One of the few public parks in Venice.

voyage.name: Bacaro Quebrado
voyage.content: Cosy tavern

voyage.name: Arcicchetti Bakaro
voyage.content: A bistro

voyage.name: Il Refolo
voyage.price: Pizza about €10, four-course meal with wine €60
voyage.address: Ramo Quinto Gallion O del Pezzetto, 1459
voyage.content: Nice restaurant at a small piazza. Very good pizza as well as a decent menu.

voyage.name: Osteria Ae Cravate
voyage.content: This little restaurant is frequented by the professors of the nearby university. Warm welcome and a good eat. Try their raw artichoke salad or their fish of the day.

voyage.name: Osteria Mocenigo
voyage.content: Little restaurant frequented by locals. Be sure to try their antipasti. Excellent desserts too.

voyage.name: Pasticceria Rio Marin
voyage.content: Coffee shop that serves excellent tiramisùs.

voyage.name: Gelateria Alaska
voyage.content: Ice cream made with natural ingredients by Carlo Pistacchi, not only the owner but an artist, a poet and a philosopher.

voyage.name: Osteria da Filo
voyage.content: An excellent place to fill up on some aperitifs and meet the local student crowd. Aperol Spritz is €2.50, a bargain for being in central Venice. The bar also hosts live music from time to time.

voyage.name: Bacareto da Lele
voyage.content: A Venetian institution that's been around since 1968. This minuscule bar serves cheap wine, a small glass is just one euro, and excellent cichetti to go along. Queuing is the norm, but the bartenders are very quick and you'll be served in no time. A great place to rub shoulders with the real Venetians.

voyage.name: Hotel Carlton on the Grand Canal
voyage.content: Large hotel, just across the Grand Canal from the railway station.

voyage.name: Hotel San Cassiano
voyage.price: From €60 in January to €200+ in peak periods

voyage.name: Doge's Palace
voyage.hours: Nov to Mar 08:30 to 17:30, Apr to Oct 08:30 to 19:00, closed Jan 1 and Dec 25
voyage.content: Don't miss the guided tour named Secret Itinerary, which will let you discover the part of the palace where the city's administration worked, as well as Casanova's jail and the wonderful five hundred year old roof structure. A MUVE museum.

voyage.name: Bell tower of St. Mark
voyage.content: The current tower dates from 1912; an exact replica of the previous tower which collapsed in 1902. The top of the tower offers great views of Venice and the lagoon.

voyage.name: Clock tower
voyage.content: Having been closed for restoration for many years, the restored astronomical clock is now visible. The fascinating tour of the clock mechanism (and rooftop bell) can only be visited on a guided tour, in English: M-W at 10:00 and 11:00, on other days at 14:00 and 15:00, in French M-W at 14:00 and 15:00, advance reservation required online or by phone at +39 041 5209070. A MUVE museum.

voyage.name: Ponte di Rialto
voyage.content: The bridge has become one of Venice's most recognizable icons and has a history that spans over 800 years. Today's Rialto Bridge was completed in 1591 and was used to replace a wooden bridge that collapsed in 1524.

voyage.name: Saint Mark's Basilica
voyage.price: Admission to the basilica is free, however, the museum upstairs costs €5 and to view the high altar and treasury costs €2 and €3 respectively
voyage.content: Saint Mark's Basilica is on the Piazza San Marco and is one of the highlights of a visit to Venice. As with most churches in Italy, you must be dressed appropriately to be allowed in; this means no short skirts or bare shoulders. You are not allowed to carry large bags or rucksacks inside, sometimes even small daypacks may need to be deposited. Storage is available just around the corner from the main entrance (free

voyage.name: Basilica San Giorgio Maggiore
voyage.price: For the bell tower: €6, reduced rate €4 (students and 65+)
voyage.content: Designed by Andrea Palladio and build 1566-1610. Very nice views of Venice from the bell tower.

voyage.name: S. Salvatore
voyage.content: Includes the tomb of Caterina Cornaro, Queen of Cyprus (1454-1510).

voyage.name: Correr Museum
voyage.hours: Nov 1 to Mar 31: 10:00-17:00, Apr 1 to Oct 31: 10:00-19:00, closed Dec 25, Jan 1
voyage.address: Piazza San Marco, Ala Napoleonica, San Marco 52
voyage.content: Interesting collection of globes, starting from the 16th century. There is also an only library hall, an archeological museum of Roman antiques and an important picture gallery. The museum offers a tour of Venetian history. Remarkable painting gallery with masterpieces of the 14th to 16th centuries from Venice, works of the Venetian sculpture Canova, studies on urban development and social life. At the end of your vi

voyage.name: Palazzo Grassi
voyage.hours: Mon Wed-Sun 10:00-19:00. Last admission 1 hr before closing
voyage.content: Contemporary art museum. Temporary exhibitions from François Pinault's Collection.

voyage.name: Palazzo Fortuny
voyage.content: Collection of paintings and lamps. A MUVE museum.

voyage.name: Telecom Italia Future Centre
voyage.content: Centre dedicated to telecommunication technology. The building complex includes an adjacent church with important works of art, the Refectory (which is a conference hall today), Renaissance cloisters and a small museum focusing on the evolution of the telephone in the last 100 years.

voyage.name: Scala Contarini del Bovolo
voyage.address: Corte del Riso o del Bovolo, San Marco 4303
voyage.content: A cylindrical tower with a spiralling series of arches, among the most characteristic examples of Venetian architecture at the period of transition from Gothic to Renaissance styles. From the top there are great panoramic views of the city.

voyage.name: Music Museum
voyage.address: Chiesa di S.Maurizio, Campo di S.Marizio, San Marco 2603
voyage.content: Beautiful church, collection of musical instruments, Venetian Baroque paintings. Interpreti Veneziani, the creators of the Music Museum, also offer concerts in the nearby San Vidal church.

voyage.name: Archaeological Museum
voyage.content: Collection of ancient Greek and Roman sculptures, Egyptian, Assyrian and Babylonian artefacts.

voyage.name: St.Mark's Basilica Museum
voyage.content: Visit the famous bronze horses.

voyage.name: Marciana National Library
voyage.alt: Sala Monumentale della Biblioteca Nazionale Marciana
voyage.content: Buildings by Sansovino, most important collection of books in Venice.

voyage.name: Giorgio Cini Foundation
voyage.content: Multi-functional centre in an old Benedictine dormitory, the heart of the Foundation's library complex

voyage.name: La Fenice Theatre
voyage.price: Tours: adults €10, students up to 26 and seniors over 65 €7, children up to 6 free. Slightly cheaper if purchased as part of a combined ticket with the Doge's palace. Performances €10-380
voyage.content: One of the best opera houses in the world. The theatre is an identical reconstruction (rebuilt in 2003) of the previous theatre building that burned down in 1996. Tickets for opera, ballet, and symphony performances are available at the theatre, various locations around the city, or by phone . You can visit this historic theatre with an audioguide (good explanations in several languages).

voyage.name: Ateneo San Basso
voyage.content: Classical concerts.

voyage.name: Chiesa San Vidal
voyage.content: Classical concerts by Interpreti Veneziani. They also run the nearby Music Museum in the nearby San Maurizio church.

voyage.name: Scuola Grande di S.Teodoro
voyage.content: Opera and concert performances.

voyage.name: Venetia Studium
voyage.address: Calle Larga XXII Marzo, San Marco 2428
voyage.content: Fine velvets and silks of every imaginable color are woven into delicate evening bags, scarves and pillows. The Company Venetia Studium produces in the Island the worldwide famous Fortuny Lamps

voyage.name: T Fondaco dei Tedeschi
voyage.content: Luxury duty-free shopping centre, housed in the historic Fondaco dei Tedeschi building where German merchants had there trading post for centuries.

voyage.name: L’Isola
voyage.address: Calle de le Botteghe, San Marco 2970

voyage.name: Bar Ducale
voyage.content: A bistro

voyage.name: We Love Italy fresh pasta to go - Rialto
Ristorante Al Conte Pescaor
voyage.content: Cozy restaurant with a terrace serving fish dishes and sea food pasta

voyage.name: Da Cherubino
voyage.content: Italian dishes.

voyage.name: Osteria Da Carla
voyage.content: An Italian restaurant

voyage.name: Antico Martini
voyage.content: A luxury restaurant, favorite among the famous names of culture and business, the Antico Martini also attracts expert gourmets and famous personalities since the 1800s who come to enjoy unforgettable flavors. Beautiful detail and restaurant decor, romantic atmosphere. The site has been a restaurant since 1720, with the venue being open since 1952.

voyage.name: Restaurant La Caravella
voyage.hours: Open every day all year round
voyage.content: Historical place near St. Mark's Square, known since the 1960s, it has become a must if you like traditions. Offers some typical dishes and a large selection of wines. From May to September service is in a traditional courtyard.

voyage.name: Caffe Quadri
voyage.content: Opposite Caffè Florian, with similar prices.

voyage.name: Bistrot de Venise
voyage.content: Restaurant, cultural and enogastronomical meetings.

voyage.name: Devils Forest Pub
voyage.address: Calle dei Stagneri o de la Fava
voyage.content: A traditional English style pub with a very fun atmosphere. It is located near the Rialto Bridge and tucked into a small alley near the Disney Store.

voyage.name: Caffè Florian
voyage.content: On the extravagant side there is Caffè Florian, on Piazza San Marco. It claims to be the oldest coffee house still in operation, established in 1720. The interior is about a century newer, and brings an exclusive setting for a cup of coffee, even if sitting outside overlooking the entire piazza and its surroundings may be a better choice on a nice summer day. The café has its own outdoor orchestra playing an assortme

voyage.name: Harry's Bar-Ristorante
voyage.content: The Bellini-cocktail was invented here. Ernest Hemingway was one of the most famous guests. Very pricy!

voyage.name: Bed and Breakfast Venice Ca' del Pozzo
voyage.content: Completely restructured in 2003, in the characteristic Campo San Maurizio.

voyage.name: Ai Do Mori
voyage.content: As close as it gets to Piazza San Marco, but on the second and third floor, so it still is quiet at nights. Clean and nice rooms, TV, aircon, very friendly staff.

voyage.name: Antico Fiore
voyage.content: An 18th-century building which has been carefully restored.

voyage.name: Astoria
voyage.content: 2-star hotel. It has Wi-Fi at a fee and rooms from €70.

voyage.name: Ca' Contarini
voyage.address: Calle dei Orbi (Corte de la Vida), San Marco 3025
voyage.content: A small, quiet establishment in a five hundred year old building. Both shared and private rooms are available, no curfew-lockouts, including free Wifi, coffee/tea, and light breakfast.

voyage.name: Ca' Rialto
voyage.content: In a building overlooking the Grand Canal and Rialto Bridge.

voyage.name: Hotel Serenissima
voyage.content: Completely refurbished at the start of 2007 and is a one-minute walk from the Piazza San Marco.

voyage.name: Ateneo Hotel Venice
voyage.price: Rooms start at around €120 depending on season
voyage.content: 3-star hotel close to Basilica San Marco.

voyage.name: Alcyone Hotel Venice
voyage.content: Its 26 bedrooms are divided in single, double, triple and superior. All with en suite services, shower, telephone, satellite TV and air conditioning.

voyage.name: Antica Casa Coppo
voyage.content: Classic Venetian styled rooms starting at €100 a night. Near the Rialto Bridge. Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Antico Casin Locanda
voyage.content: A refined example of contemporary design, located close to Saint Mark's Square. Doubles from €90.

voyage.name: Domus Ciliota
voyage.content: A 5-10 minute walk from San Marco's Square. The hotel has over fifty clean, basic, air-conditioned rooms all with shower and WC. The 24-hr reception is English speaking. There is an area for leaving baggage after you've checked out. Single rooms are €70-85 and doubles are €100-110 including breakfast.

voyage.name: Hotel Ala
voyage.address: Campo Santa Maria dei Gigli, San Marco 2494
voyage.content: Eggs and broiled tomatoes with cheese for breakfast. Rooms were a typical size but clean, comfortable and quiet. They have turndown service at night, a pleasant surprise.

voyage.name: Hotel All’Angelo Venice
voyage.content: Run by the same family since 1924 in a 17th-century building close to St Marks Basilica. Comfortable and stylishly decorated rooms with a double somewhere in the region of €150.

voyage.name: Hotel Antico Panada
voyage.content: Has rooms decorated in an 18th-century Venetian style.

voyage.name: Hotel Becher
voyage.content: This 18th-century hotel enhanced by the most modern amenities, charming atmosphere and impeccable service. Single rooms from €70, doubles €110 and triples from €170.

voyage.name: Hotel Firenze Venice
voyage.price: Rooms start at around €120 a double/twin
voyage.content: On a side street of Piazza San Marco, and offers bright and comfortable rooms.

voyage.name: Hotel Lisbona Venice
voyage.content: Just in front of Piazza San Marco, three star rooms decorated in the grand Venetian style. Double rooms are usually around €140.

voyage.name: Hotel Montecarlo Venice
voyage.price: Rooms start at around €130 a double
voyage.content: 3-star superior rooms and services one hundred yards from the entrance to Basilica San Marco.

voyage.name: Hotel San Giorgio
voyage.price: Single rooms from €60, doubles from €90, triples from €120
voyage.address: Rio Terà della Mandola, San Marco 3781
voyage.content: The hotel is between Campo Sant'Angelo and Campo Manin in an antique Gothic palace bought by Mariano Fortuny.

voyage.name: Hotel San Moise Venice
voyage.price: Starting in the region of €120-140 for a double room
voyage.content: 3-star hotel behind Piazza San Marco and the Basilica.

voyage.name: Pagan Luxury House
voyage.content: According to their website, there is a €10 per night discount for booking directly with them.

voyage.name: Novecento Boutique Hotel
voyage.content: Has 9 rooms featuring original furniture and tapestries from both the Mediterranean and the Far East.

voyage.name: Palazzina Grassi Hotel
voyage.content: First Italian hotel designed by Philippe Starck, the only one in Venice. In the centre, near the Basilica dei Santi Giovanni e Paolo. Saint Mark's Square is a short walk away.

voyage.name: Duodo Palace Hotel
voyage.content: Four-star luxury hotel.

voyage.name: Hotel Al Codega
voyage.address: Corte del Forno Vecchio, San Marco 4435
voyage.content: In a picturesque little ‘cortile’ (courtyard), which is a short walk from Piazza San Marco.

voyage.name: Hotel Dei Dragomanni
voyage.address: Calle del Dose da Ponte, San Marco 2711
voyage.content: 4-star hotel in an ancient Venetian palazzo.

voyage.name: Corte di Gabriela
voyage.content: Corte di Gabriela is a 4-star boutique hotel in Venice in an elegant nineteenth-century building, overlooking the canals of the San Marco district. It has a few suites, each different from the others.

voyage.name: Hotel Bauer Palazzo
voyage.content: Historic luxury hotel facing the Grand Canal. Hotel Bauer has been around since 1880.

voyage.name: The Gritti Palace
voyage.content: Housed in the Palazzo Pisani Gritti, facing the Grand Canal, this hotel was once the private residency of a 16th century dodge. It has been a hotel since 1895

voyage.name: Lace Museum
voyage.hours: Apr-Oct: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00; Nov-Mar: Tue-Sun 10:00-17:00; ticket office closes 30 min earlier; closed Mon, Dec 25, Jan 1, May 1 closed
voyage.content: There is a small lace museum called Museo del Merletto. Opinions on it vary from "not much to see" to "I didn't think I was interested in lace, but I spent 90 minutes in there". A MUVE museum.

voyage.name: Trattoria da Romano
voyage.content: Famous people, including royalty, visited the place. The walls are covered with their photo's.

en.title: Galleria Giorgio Franchetti alla Ca' d'Oro
Palazzo Benedetti a Santa Sofia, Venice
